newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat meets Israeli defence chief in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Arafat meets Israeli defence chief in Gaza.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai met on Sunday night at their border to hammer out details of a Hebron agreement, witnesses said.

"Tonight's meeting will concentrate on the substance of certain security issues. President Arafat and Minister Mordechai will be discussing and trying to bridge the gap," chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told reporters beforehand.

Israeli and PLO officials have said they expect Arafat and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to sign an agreement giving the Palestinians control of 80 percent of Hebron by Tuesday, the end of the year.
Hebron is the last of seven occupied West Bank cities Israel agreed to give self-rule under an agreement signed with the PLO in 1995. The PLO took over much of the Gaza Strip in 1994.
U.S. President Bill Clinton's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross was due back in the region on Monday to mediate any last-minute snags and attend the signing.

Security concerns have held up the handover in Hebron, including demands by Netanyahu for additional measures he says are needed to protect the 400 Jewish settlers in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.
